newsitem.title: USA: TransAmerican Energy to offer $1.53 bln in debt.
newsitem.headline: TransAmerican Energy to offer $1.53 bln in debt.

text.p: TransAmerican Energy Corp said Wednesday that it is beginning an offering of $1.53 billion in long-term debt.

The company said it will offer the debt in the form of $425 million of senior secured notes due 2002 and $1.105 billion of senior secured discount notes due 2002, resulting in gross proceeds of about $1.3 billion for the company.
TransAmerican said the offering will help recapitalization of its two operating subsidiaries, TransTexas Gas Corp and TransAmerican Refining Corp.

Separately, the company also said it plans to launch a buyback of up to $371 million of its common stock and that it is in exclusive talks to sell its TransTexas Transmission Corp subsidiary for expected consideration of about $1.1 billion.
Additionally, it said it is beginning a tender offer for the outstanding warrants to buy common stock in TransAmerican Refining at $3 per warrant. It said the offer will expire June 12.
It also said it plans to begin a tender offer to buy all its outstanding $340 million of guaranteed first mortgage discount notes due 2002 at 110 percent of the accreted value to the purchase date.
It said it would begin a tender for all $100 million of guaranteed first mortgage notes due 2002 at 110 percent of principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest.
Finally, the company said it would being a tender to buy all its outstanding $800 million of 11-1/2 senior secured notes due 2002 at 111-1/2 percent of the principal amount.
